senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to cut off, separate,] to fence in, mark off. Y. Ab. Zar. IV, 43ᶜ, sq. כל שהוא סָג וכ׳ any stone that is put up to mark the sea-shore or the roads.
units: Y. M. Kat. I, 80ᶜ פירצה שהיא סָגָה וכ׳ a fence which, though broken, still bars the ground behind it (from falling out); Y. Shebi. III, end, 34ᵈ; a. e.—Trnsf. (v. סְיָג a. גָּדַר) to guard against trespassing a law, to make a prohibition more restrictive; to exaggerate.

<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 1:7">Ab. d’R. N. ch. I</cite> <he>סייג שסָג … לדבריו</he> (v. ed. Schechter) the guard which Adam set to his words (by adding the prohibition to touch the tree of knowledge).
<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 1:7">Ib.</cite> <he>אם סג אדם לדבריו וכ׳</he> if a person exaggerates his words, he cannot abide by them.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:14">Koh. R. to V, 14</cite> <he>והיה מס׳ וכ׳</he> it (the vineyard) was fenced in on all sides.

<cite ref="Shabbat 85a:2">Sabb. 85ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 19:14">Deut. XIX, 14</cite>) <he>גבול … לא תַסִּיג</he> do not remove the landmark which those before thee (the Canaanites) have set.
